overview.headline: Constant speed flight and how ground speed sets aircraft range

keyPoints.point: Cruising airplane holds constant speed and level flight when lift is equal to weight and thrust is equal to drag
keyPoints.quote: in which the lift is equal to the weight, and the thrust is equal to the drag.

keyPoints.point: Ground speed remains constant while wind speed stays constant for cruising aircraft
keyPoints.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.

keyPoints.point: Distance flown equals ground speed times time aloft for constant ground speed
keyPoints.quote: the distance flown is equal to the ground speed times the time aloft.

keyPoints.point: Maximum time aloft is limited by fuel load and sets maximum range with ground speed
keyPoints.quote: There is a time limit, or maximum time, that an airplane can stay aloft, which is usually determined by the fuel load.
